tasks.task: Write first replies to enquiries by type

items.when: When an enquiry arrives and the reply must give the answer, one or two questions and a next step
When the same kinds of enquiry keep coming and you want one reply per type to reuse
When you want a second draft that qualifies the enquiry and offers real meeting times
When the inbox is full and each new email needs ranking and a checked draft to approve
When replies go unopened, to try several subject lines that stay clear
Before a reply template is saved, to cut it and get a send or fix verdict
When the reply opens with the business and its history instead of what the buyer asked

tasks.task: Write hold reminders and quote follow-ups

items.when: When a buyer holds a date or has a quote and then goes quiet
Before writing the series, to compare three plans for it, each with its first email
When one follow-up must become four, each with a new reason, one ask and a stop rule
Before chasing, to judge whether the buyer doubts you, is still comparing or fears choosing
When a big booking has stalled and you want easy-yes questions and a calm message
Before the series is loaded, to check each email is short and has one ask

tasks.task: Build a quote or proposal with up to three options

items.when: When you have the buyer's brief and the rate card and need options, inclusions and the total
When the quote must go into the client's own branded template from call notes or photos
When the buyer should see good, better and best versions with a reason for each price
When you start from a call and want the follow-up, costing, margin check and dates in order
When the buyer needs a dated list of steps from yes to signed, to share with them
Before sending, to read the quote as the buyer and list what they would still have to ask

tasks.task: Check a quote's maths, fees and terms before it goes

items.when: When a quote or package page is ready and needs a second look at sums, fees and missing details
When the quote includes catering, to match the order to the quote and event details
When the booking terms confuse buyers and need a plain-words version beside the quote
When a supplier's or buyer's terms are attached and a clause looks risky

tasks.task: Set up the enquiry-to-booking process

items.when: When enquiries wait too long, replies vary by sender, holds lapse or quotes go out wrong
When calls or viewings should be booked online with qualifying questions and prep emails
When people enquire months ahead and need useful information before they are ready
When the steps and who does each must be written so a new person can follow them

tasks.task: Hand a confirmed sale to the delivery team

items.when: When a sale is confirmed and the delivery team needs everything that was sold and promised
When the details sit in a long email thread and must become one handoff sheet
When a buyer signs, pays a deposit or sends a purchase order and the steps after must not slip
When a colleague takes over your open bookings and needs a note to run from on day one
When the sale is a hotel group booking with deposits, rates and requests to check
Before confirming a date to the buyer, to see whether the team has the hours

tasks.task: Write order, backorder, delay and substitution messages

items.when: When a trade order line is out of stock, late or needs a substitute and the buyer needs options
When buyers keep asking where their order is and need a set of updates and a delay script
When freight is late, lost or damaged and you need next steps and the customer message
When planning the full set from acknowledgement to dispatch, to compare three ways to run it
Before a delay message goes, to check every new date and promise in it can be kept

tasks.task: Run the weekly CRM hygiene sweep

items.when: When you need duplicates, deals with no next step and stuck deals listed with fixes
When the pipeline report cannot be trusted or a busy season or price change is coming
When you want a second pass for missing fields, stale dates and stage mismatches
When emails and calls have not been logged and deals need updating from them
When the owner wants what changed this week and which bookings to act on today

tasks.task: Write packages, pricing page and brochure copy

items.when: Before writing, to set the tiers, what each includes and the price points
When each package needs a name, value framing and payment terms
When the packages page needs a hero, value points, proof and answers to doubts
When the client should see three different openings for the page as real screens
When a package line could describe any venue or studio, to get a true, picturable rewrite
Before the page goes live, to confirm a buyer can enquire or book from it today

tasks.task: Write a listing description for a property or space

items.when: When the listing headline is flat, to compare several honest angles on the same home
When the description is a list of rooms and needs one simple, concrete idea to lead with
When a line such as "stunning and spacious" could fit any listing
Before publishing, so sizes, distances and school or transport claims each have a source
When the listing names features and never shows what living there is like

tasks.task: Plan open-house invitations, tours and their follow-up

items.when: When viewing or tour requests need a reply that books the slot and says what to bring
When an open house or showcase needs a plan to fill it and follow up after
When the invitation needs several subject lines to choose from
After the open house or tour, to follow up by what each visitor asked about
Before the invitation is sent, to cut it and check the date, place and ask are clear

tasks.task: Write a day-by-day itinerary and trip quote cover note

items.when: When you have dates, needs and budget and need daily stops, breaks and alternatives with sources
When the traveller could go two ways, such as slow and few stops or fast and many, with costs
When the itinerary needs a quote that states what is and is not included
Before sending, so opening times, transfer times and entry rules each have a dated source

tasks.task: Write an event-day timeline or run sheet for your part

items.when: When the timeline must start from what was sold: times, numbers, rooms and extras
When you need a run sheet from arrival to exit, who does what and what the venue must confirm
When food is part of the day, to check the order against the timeline and guest numbers

tasks.task: Write a weekly client update or minutes from notes

items.when: When a seller or client is owed a weekly note on what was done, what is stuck and what is next
When rough notes from a client meeting must become decisions and actions with owners
When a call just ended and you need the follow-up email and the CRM updates to approve
When a client complains they never hear from you and update dates need agreeing

tasks.task: Write thank-you, review and referral requests

items.when: After delivery, to write the thank-you and plan when to stay in touch and ask for a referral
When you want a testimonial and the client needs three easy questions to answer
When public reviews matter and you need when to ask, the wording and how to answer a bad one
When the request needs a few subject lines to pick from
Before the request goes, to check it is short and asks for one thing
When contact stops the day the invoice is paid

tasks.task: Write a client prep guide, FAQ or welcome pack

items.when: When clients ask the same questions before every booking and the answers should be on one page
When you want the awkward questions clients will ask found and answered before they ask
When the guide is for a shoot and the client needs to know what to bring and expect
When the pack must explain deposit, cancellation and change terms in plain words
When the guide is drafted, to read it as a first-time client and list what is still unclear

tasks.task: Build a set of canned replies and macros

items.when: When the set should start with one first reply for each enquiry type
Before writing, to capture the team's senders, reply voice and rules in one saved guide
When saved replies sound like a form letter and buyers can tell
When you want a differently built version of a reply to compare before saving it
When the set is drafted, to find where replies drift from the business's voice

tasks.task: Write hard replies: a no, a complaint, a price rise

items.when: When you must turn down a date, a discount or extra work and keep the buyer's trust
When a client asks for more than they booked, to compare the request with what was agreed
When an angry message arrives and the reply must fix what it can and promise nothing false
When the complaint is from a hotel or venue guest and you want a second reply with a fair fix
When rates go up and booked or regular clients need a letter that keeps most of them
Before a complaint reply goes, to check each promise and the tone

tasks.task: Write deposit and payment reminders

items.when: When a held date lapses unless the deposit arrives and the buyer needs a clear reminder
When a balance is overdue and the reminder must keep the customer's goodwill
When a UK trade invoice is late and you want the legal interest and fee worked out
When setting the reminder series, to compare three ways to pace and word it
Before reminders go, to check any date, hold or consequence stated is one you will keep

tasks.task: Write the order desk procedure from quote to dispatch

items.when: When the procedure should follow the steps from confirmed order to delivery
When you need a flowchart, who does what and the written steps with the edge cases
When a small studio needs its procedures, owners, tools and suppliers in one operating plan

tasks.task: Design an enquiry, brief or trade account form

items.when: When you need the questions that get what the buyer knows and you do not
When the form is long, such as a trade account application, and needs stages and conditions
When a booking page with a few questions might replace the form altogether

always.when: Before anything goes to a buyer, to catch typos and a name or date written two ways
When a message states a price, a date, a capacity or a rule, so each has a source
When a reply must sound like the business and you have its voice guide

helpers.when: When the booking needs a full event plan, suppliers and a run sheet for the whole day
When the buyer wants a long formal proposal or sends a tender
When complaints and after-sale questions need a help centre and macros of their own
When a property sale moves from offer to closing and the paperwork must be tracked
When a trade order has freight, customs or carrier problems behind the delay
When the CRM needs new stages, fields or automations, not a weekly tidy

gaps: No library item writes a property listing description or checks it against fair housing and listing rules
No library item writes an open-house invitation pack or a venue tour script
No library item writes a wedding-day or event-day timeline for one supplier's part
No library item writes a travel quote with inclusions, supplier terms and package travel rules, or a destination guide
No library item writes trade order acknowledgements, confirmations, backorder or substitution messages
No library item builds a trade account opening form or a welcome pack for new trade accounts
No library item checks a quote's maths: line totals, mandatory fees, tax and deposit
No library item manages date holds: who holds what, when each lapses and who to chase
No library item builds a canned reply or macro set by enquiry type
No library item writes a client prep guide for a shoot, a wedding or a venue hire
No library item writes a weekly update from an agent to a property seller
